classification.difficultyReason: Requires two possible placements of the given angle and an explanation of the resulting alternatives.

content.prompt: One of the angles in an isosceles triangle is $80^{\circ}$. Work out the sizes of the other two angles.

answer.worked:
If $80^{\circ}$ is the angle between the equal sides, let each remaining angle be $x^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+80&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of a triangle)}\\2x&=100\\x&=50\end{align*}$$
The other angles are $50^{\circ}$ and $50^{\circ}$.

If $80^{\circ}$ is one of the equal angles, let the remaining unequal angle be $y^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}y+80+80&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of a triangle)}\\y+160&=180\\y&=20\end{align*}$$
The other angles are $80^{\circ}$ and $20^{\circ}$.

children.prompt: Explain why there are two possible sets of answers.

answer.short: The $80^{\circ}$ angle may be the unequal angle or one of the two equal angles.
answer.worked: The question does not specify whether $80^{\circ}$ is the unequal angle or one of the two equal angles. Both possibilities give valid triangles, with other angles $50^{\circ},50^{\circ}$ or $80^{\circ},20^{\circ}$.
